description: 20 distinct 60-question Language papers and 20 distinct 15-question practice sets, original content with 317-word spelling bank. Automated answer and uniqueness checks passed. Human editorial spot checks conducted; continued review recommended.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: Neither the chair nor the analysts who drafted the report ___ prepared to endorse it.
options: has been
were
was
is
questions.explanation: The nearer plural noun requires the plural verb were.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: Each of the findings that the analysts discussed ___ supported by independent evidence.
options: were
have been
is
are
questions.explanation: The singular distributive head each governs is despite the intervening plural phrase.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: By the time Anika presented the report, the review team ___ its sources.
options: has already checked
will check
is checking
had already checked
questions.explanation: Past perfect marks a completed event before another past event.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: After reviewing the contradictory evidence, ___.
options: the analysts revised their interpretation
a discrepancy became apparent
the report was amended
the result seemed doubtful
questions.explanation: The people who performed the reviewing must immediately follow the opening modifier.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: The revised interpretation was more comprehensive than ___.
options: the archive that stored the document
that in the earlier report
the previous chair
the original analysts
questions.explanation: The construction compares interpretations with interpretations, not people or institutions.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: If Anika ___ responsible for the report, the chair would seek independent confirmation.
options: has been
is
were
will be
questions.explanation: Were expresses an unreal present condition in conventional formal usage.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: The report may be accepted only if the analysts approve it. What can be inferred?
options: Their approval guarantees acceptance.
Acceptance may precede approval under the stated rule.
No unapproved proposal has ever been submitted.
Their approval is necessary, not necessarily sufficient.
questions.explanation: Only if specifies a necessary condition and does not guarantee success.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: Which sentence identifies Anika as the person who actually inspected the evidence?
options: After inspecting the evidence, Anika informed the chair.
Anika informed the chair after she inspected it.
After she inspected it, Anika informed the chair.
The chair and Anika discussed the findings after she inspected it.
questions.explanation: The introductory modifier clearly identifies its agent in the first sentence; the other references are ambiguous.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: Which sentence means that the analysts revised no section except the conclusion?
options: The analysts revised the only conclusion of the report.
The analysts revised only the conclusion of the report.
Only the analysts revised the conclusion of the report.
The analysts only revised the conclusion of the report.
questions.explanation: Only immediately before the object narrows what was revised.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: Which sentence correctly connects two independent clauses with a conjunctive adverb?
options: The report was persuasive; nevertheless the chair requested more evidence.
The report was persuasive nevertheless; the chair requested more evidence.
The report was persuasive; nevertheless, the chair requested more evidence.
The report was persuasive, nevertheless, the chair requested more evidence.
questions.explanation: A semicolon separates the independent clauses and a comma follows nevertheless.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: The number of analysts assigned to the task ___ increased since September.
options: have
were
are
has
questions.explanation: The singular head number takes has, despite the plural noun in its complement.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: Which version accurately compares the number of unsupported claims?
options: The revised report contained fewer unsupported claims.
The revised report contained less unsupported claims.
The revised report contained least unsupported claims.
The revised report contained much fewer unsupported claims.
questions.explanation: Claims are countable, so fewer is the standard comparative.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, A number of researchers ___ raised concerns about the proposed interpretation.
options: was
have
has
is
questions.explanation: A number of followed by a plural noun takes a plural verb.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, Either the analysts or the department head ___ required to approve the final report.
options: were
have
is
are
questions.explanation: The nearest noun head is singular, so is is correct.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, Which punctuation correctly connects the two independent clauses?
options: The evidence was incomplete, the review continued.
The evidence was incomplete: and the review continued.
The evidence was incomplete; and, the review continued.
The evidence was incomplete; the review continued.
questions.explanation: A semicolon may directly join two closely related independent clauses without a coordinating conjunction.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, Which construction uses inversion correctly after the negative adverbial?
options: Not only did the committee revise its proposal, but it also explained the change.
Not only the committee did revise its proposal, but explained also.
Not only did the committee revised its proposal but also explained.
Not only the committee had revised its proposal, but it also explaining.
questions.explanation: Negative-initial not only requires auxiliary inversion in the first clause.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, Which version uses whose as a relative possessive rather than confusing it with who is?
options: The researcher who measurements were disputed requested a review.
The researcher whose measurements were disputed requested a review.
The researcher who's measurements were disputed requested a review.
The researcher whose's measurements were disputed requested a review.
questions.explanation: Whose is a possessive relative determiner; who's means who is or who has.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, Which sentence means that the director considered just one document and no others?
options: The director only examined the revised report.
The director examined the only revised report.
The director examined only the revised report.
Only the director examined the revised report.
questions.explanation: Only modifies the immediately following object 'the revised report' to restrict the documents examined.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, Which comparison preserves the intended grammatical structure?
options: The second analysis was as more rigorous as the first.
The second analysis was so rigorous than the first.
The second analysis was most rigorous as the first.
The second analysis was as rigorous as the first analysis.
questions.explanation: The equality comparison follows as + adjective + as.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, Which quantifier correctly describes a reduced amount of uncertainty, treated as an uncountable quantity?
options: The revised model left less uncertainty.
The revised model left fewer uncertainty.
The revised model left least uncertainty than before.
The revised model left many less uncertainty.
questions.explanation: Uncertainty is mass-noun usage here, requiring less rather than fewer.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, Which sentence uses lay as a transitive verb rather than confusing it with intransitive lie?
options: The technician lies the instruments on the table yesterday.
The technician laid the instruments on the table before leaving.
The technician lay the instruments on the table yesterday.
The technician lain the instruments on the table yesterday.
questions.explanation: Laid is the past tense of transitive lay and takes the direct object instruments.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, Which choice uses complement to mean a feature that completes or enhances another?
options: The appendix provides evidence that complement's the argument.
The appendix provides evidence that compliment the argument.
The appendix provides evidence that complements the argument.
The appendix provides evidence that compliments the argument.
questions.explanation: The verb complement means to complete or enhance; compliment means praise.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, Which sentence consistently reports a past claim without an illogical tense shift?
options: The editor said that the committee will have reviewed the evidence yesterday.
The editor said that the committee review the evidence before it published.
The editor said that the committee had reviews the evidence before publishing.
The editor said that the committee had reviewed the evidence before publishing.
questions.explanation: Past reporting combines naturally with a past perfect for an earlier action.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, Which sentence correctly treats the relative clause as additional, nonrestrictive information about a known group?
options: The three finalists, who had all submitted their work, awaited the decision.
The three finalists who had all submitted their work, awaited the decision.
The three finalists, who had all submitted their work awaited the decision.
The three finalists who had all submitted their work awaited, the decision.
questions.explanation: A nonrestrictive clause is bracketed by commas and does not select only some of the known finalists.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, Which version makes the introductory action's agent unambiguous?
options: Having read the transcript, the report's conclusions changed.
Having reviewed the transcript, the historian corrected the chronology.
Having reviewed the transcript, the chronology was corrected.
After studying the archive, a discrepancy appeared.
questions.explanation: The historian is the following subject and therefore performs the reviewing.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, Which version appropriately uses were to express an unreal present condition?
options: The committee spoke as if the outcome had certain yesterday.
The committee spoke as if the outcome be already certainty.
The committee spoke as if the outcome were already certain.
The committee spoke as if the outcome will already certain.
questions.explanation: Were marks a contrary-to-fact or hypothetical state in formal usage.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, Neither of the proposed interpretations ___ supported by the available data.
options: are
were
have
is
questions.explanation: Neither is grammatically singular in this formal construction.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, Which question correctly uses whom in a formal object position?
options: Whom did the panel invite to testify?
Whom submitted the final report?
Whom was responsible for the analysis?
Whom have been approved for the hearing?
questions.explanation: Whom is the object of invite; the other questions need subject-case who.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, Which punctuation correctly marks the introductory dependent clause?
options: Although the data, appeared consistent the team requested replication.
Although the data appeared consistent, the team requested replication.
Although the data appeared consistent the team, requested replication.
Although, the data appeared consistent the team requested replication.
questions.explanation: A dependent opening clause is followed by a comma before the main clause.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, Which sentence maintains parallel objects with not only...but also?
options: The team evaluated not only the methods but also evaluating the assumptions.
The team evaluated not only the methods but also to assess the assumptions.
The team evaluated not only the methods but also the underlying assumptions.
The team not only evaluated the methods but also the underlying assumptions.
questions.explanation: Both correlatives introduce parallel noun phrases serving as objects of evaluated.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: A preliminary observation in astronomy was positive. Which conclusion is appropriately calibrated?
options: One positive result demonstrates a permanent causal mechanism.
The evidence is encouraging, but different settings should be tested before generalizing.
The observation proves the technique works everywhere.
All alternative explanations are now impossible.
questions.explanation: A preliminary observation supports a provisional inference rather than a universal conclusion.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: Which evidence would best establish that a new procedure reduced errors in astronomy?
options: A description of the room where the procedure originated.
The number of pages in the final report.
A comparison of verified error rates under comparable conditions.
An announcement praising the procedure's designers.
questions.explanation: Comparable error-rate measurements directly test the alleged improvement.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: Which sentence makes a concession without abandoning the argument?
options: The intervention costs money, so the idea must be rejected.
The intervention cannot possibly have drawbacks.
The intervention is correct because its supporters are enthusiastic.
Although implementation may be costly, a limited pilot could test whether the benefits justify that expense.
questions.explanation: The concession admits a legitimate cost while proposing evidence to evaluate the trade-off.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: Which additional method would most reduce uncertainty about a causal claim in astronomy?
options: Identify selection effects and plausible confounding variables.
Replace the results section with a more confident abstract.
Repeat the same conclusion in several paragraphs.
Remove inconvenient outliers without documenting them.
questions.explanation: Addressing confounding and selection can distinguish a causal relationship from a misleading association.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: Which transition best introduces a limitation following positive results?
options: Similarly, no further investigation is necessary.
Nevertheless, the data cover too short a period to establish a lasting trend.
Therefore, every other hypothesis is impossible.
In other words, a favorable result guarantees universal success.
questions.explanation: Nevertheless marks a meaningful qualification to apparently promising evidence.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy full-paper case: Which finding would independently corroborate a disputed historical claim in astronomy?
options: Several summaries quote the same anonymous assertion.
A popular account asserts the story is interesting.
An unrelated dated record supports the same chronology.
The original author repeats the claim in a later paragraph.
questions.explanation: Independent supporting material is stronger corroboration than restating the same unsupported source.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, What unstated assumption is required to infer public opinion from a volunteer survey?
options: All respondents prefer answering surveys.
The survey report contains at least two paragraphs.
The researchers interviewed every official.
The volunteers adequately represent the wider population.
questions.explanation: Extrapolating from volunteers assumes they do not differ systematically from the broader public.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, Which interpretation avoids the post hoc fallacy when a policy change precedes an improvement?
options: The sequence is consistent with causation but does not establish it without ruling out alternative causes.
The earlier policy change necessarily caused the improvement.
Every improvement must follow from the most recent change.
Temporal order invalidates all observational evidence.
questions.explanation: Temporal sequence is necessary for many causal accounts but cannot alone identify the cause.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, Which sentence fairly represents an opponent's strongest concern before responding to it?
options: The cost is irrelevant because the proposal is well intentioned.
Critics argue that the cost may burden smaller institutions; a staged rollout could test affordability.
Critics oppose the plan because they dislike all improvements.
Anyone who questions the cost is ignorant of basic facts.
questions.explanation: A fair counterargument identifies a plausible concern and supplies a relevant, proportionate response.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, Which sentence avoids a straw-man response?
options: The critic must oppose every form of scientific inquiry.
The objection is false because the critic sounds worried.
The objection concerns uncertainty in the sample, which the next study should directly address.
The critic believes no data should ever be collected.
questions.explanation: A fair rebuttal answers the actual concern about sampling rather than misrepresenting it as total opposition.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, Which evidence best supports the claim that a new scheduling policy improved access?
options: A slogan emphasizing the policy's fairness.
The director's biography and number of awards.
A description of the new meeting-room paint.
Comparable participation rates before and after adoption, separated by previously underserved groups.
questions.explanation: Access must be assessed through outcomes for affected groups, not through aspirations or peripheral details.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, What most directly addresses external validity after a promising result in one institution?
options: Replication in institutions with different populations and operating conditions.
A larger poster advertising the first trial.
An additional summary of the same initial observations.
Removing participants who disagree with the researcher's conclusion.
questions.explanation: External validity concerns whether findings hold across relevant settings and populations.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, Which transition links a paragraph of favorable evidence to a paragraph about its limits?
options: Likewise, no further evidence is needed.
Nevertheless, the study's restricted time frame prevents stronger conclusions.
Consequently, all uncertainty has disappeared.
For instance, the first result proves every outcome.
questions.explanation: Nevertheless signals a contrast between encouraging findings and a meaningful qualification.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, Which thesis is both arguable and specific?
options: There are many different opinions about library hours.
I will discuss several interesting aspects of libraries.
A limited trial of longer library hours would help students with late obligations without requiring immediate districtwide expansion.
Libraries are places where people can read.
questions.explanation: The first thesis states a defined, debatable proposal and its rationale.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, Two competing explanations fit the same results. What should the next investigation prioritize?
options: More forceful repetition of the preferred explanation.
Removal of all results that appear inconsistent.
A vote to decide which explanation sounds more persuasive.
A prediction on which the explanations disagree and a measurement able to test it.
questions.explanation: A discriminating prediction tests rival hypotheses rather than relying on rhetoric or preference.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, Which comparison best supports evaluating an intervention's effectiveness?
options: Outcomes in comparable exposed and unexposed groups, accounting for baseline differences.
A favorable anecdote collected after implementation.
The intervention's advertised purpose.
A list of names of people who designed the intervention.
questions.explanation: A controlled comparison helps separate an intervention effect from background differences.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, Which assessment of a source's reliability is most defensible?
options: Assume all old sources are inherently accurate.
Evaluate its evidence, methods, possible incentives, and independent corroboration.
Treat professional titles as sufficient proof.
Accept any source repeated frequently online.
questions.explanation: Reliability depends on traceable methods and evidence rather than authority or repetition alone.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, Which interpretation of a historical object stays within the evidence?
options: The artifact reveals the full intentions of its maker without corroboration.
The single find establishes a universal historical law.
Its presence suggests a practice at that site, but not necessarily how widespread or intentional the practice was.
The object proves every resident shared an identical belief.
questions.explanation: A local artifact supports bounded inferences and does not establish prevalence or mental states.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, When is an analogy strongest as evidence?
options: Whenever the situations have similar-sounding names.
Whenever a memorable story can be substituted for data.
When one case is popular, even if the relevant mechanisms differ.
When the two situations share the features relevant to the conclusion being drawn.
questions.explanation: A valid analogy depends on the similarity of causally or logically relevant features.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 astronomical modeling assessment, Which conclusion best synthesizes promising evidence and its stated limitations?
options: The findings justify further targeted trials, not immediate certainty about every possible application.
The hypothesis has been established in every population.
The limitations prove that the evidence is worthless.
A positive result makes methodological details unnecessary.
questions.explanation: A synthesis integrates support and qualification without overstating generality.

The three finalists, who had all submitted their work, awaited the decision.
The three finalists who had all submitted their work, awaited the decision.
The three finalists, who had all submitted their work awaited the decision.
questions.explanation: A nonrestrictive clause is bracketed by commas and does not select only some of the known finalists.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 archival scholarship assessment, Which version makes the introductory action's agent unambiguous?
options: After studying the archive, a discrepancy appeared.
Having read the transcript, the report's conclusions changed.
Having reviewed the transcript, the historian corrected the chronology.
Having reviewed the transcript, the chronology was corrected.
questions.explanation: The historian is the following subject and therefore performs the reviewing.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 archival scholarship assessment, Which version appropriately uses were to express an unreal present condition?
options: The committee spoke as if the outcome will already certain.
The committee spoke as if the outcome had certain yesterday.

The committee spoke as if the outcome were already certain.
questions.explanation: Were marks a contrary-to-fact or hypothetical state in formal usage.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 archival scholarship assessment, Neither of the proposed interpretations ___ supported by the available data.

are
were
have
questions.explanation: Neither is grammatically singular in this formal construction.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 archival scholarship assessment, Which question correctly uses whom in a formal object position?

Whom did the panel invite to testify?
Whom submitted the final report?
Whom was responsible for the analysis?
questions.explanation: Whom is the object of invite; the other questions need subject-case who.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 archival scholarship assessment, Which punctuation correctly marks the introductory dependent clause?
options: Although, the data appeared consistent the team requested replication.
Although the data, appeared consistent the team requested replication.
Although the data appeared consistent, the team requested replication.
Although the data appeared consistent the team, requested replication.
questions.explanation: A dependent opening clause is followed by a comma before the main clause.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 archival scholarship assessment, Which sentence maintains parallel objects with not only...but also?

The team evaluated not only the methods but also evaluating the assumptions.
The team evaluated not only the methods but also to assess the assumptions.
The team evaluated not only the methods but also the underlying assumptions.
questions.explanation: Both correlatives introduce parallel noun phrases serving as objects of evaluated.

questions.text: In the day 14 public policy full-paper case: A preliminary observation in public policy was positive. Which conclusion is appropriately calibrated?
options: All alternative explanations are now impossible.
One positive result demonstrates a permanent causal mechanism.
The evidence is encouraging, but different settings should be tested before generalizing.
The observation proves the technique works everywhere.
questions.explanation: A preliminary observation supports a provisional inference rather than a universal conclusion.

questions.text: In the day 14 public policy full-paper case: Which evidence would best establish that a new procedure reduced errors in public policy?
options: An announcement praising the procedure's designers.
A description of the room where the procedure originated.
The number of pages in the final report.
A comparison of verified error rates under comparable conditions.
questions.explanation: Comparable error-rate measurements directly test the alleged improvement.

questions.text: In the day 14 public policy full-paper case: Which sentence makes a concession without abandoning the argument?
options: Although implementation may be costly, a limited pilot could test whether the benefits justify that expense.
The intervention costs money, so the idea must be rejected.
The intervention cannot possibly have drawbacks.
The intervention is correct because its supporters are enthusiastic.
questions.explanation: The concession admits a legitimate cost while proposing evidence to evaluate the trade-off.

questions.text: In the day 14 public policy full-paper case: Which additional method would most reduce uncertainty about a causal claim in public policy?
options: Remove inconvenient outliers without documenting them.
Identify selection effects and plausible confounding variables.
Replace the results section with a more confident abstract.
Repeat the same conclusion in several paragraphs.
questions.explanation: Addressing confounding and selection can distinguish a causal relationship from a misleading association.

questions.text: In the day 14 public policy full-paper case: Which transition best introduces a limitation following positive results?
options: In other words, a favorable result guarantees universal success.
Similarly, no further investigation is necessary.
Nevertheless, the data cover too short a period to establish a lasting trend.
Therefore, every other hypothesis is impossible.
questions.explanation: Nevertheless marks a meaningful qualification to apparently promising evidence.

questions.text: In the day 14 public policy full-paper case: Which finding would independently corroborate a disputed historical claim in public policy?
options: The original author repeats the claim in a later paragraph.
Several summaries quote the same anonymous assertion.
A popular account asserts the story is interesting.
An unrelated dated record supports the same chronology.
questions.explanation: Independent supporting material is stronger corroboration than restating the same unsupported source.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 archival scholarship assessment, What unstated assumption is required to infer public opinion from a volunteer survey?
options: The volunteers adequately represent the wider population.
All respondents prefer answering surveys.
The survey report contains at least two paragraphs.
The researchers interviewed every official.
questions.explanation: Extrapolating from volunteers assumes they do not differ systematically from the broader public.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 archival scholarship assessment, Which interpretation avoids the post hoc fallacy when a policy change precedes an improvement?
options: Temporal order invalidates all observational evidence.
The sequence is consistent with causation but does not establish it without ruling out alternative causes.
The earlier policy change necessarily caused the improvement.
Every improvement must follow from the most recent change.
questions.explanation: Temporal sequence is necessary for many causal accounts but cannot alone identify the cause.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 archival scholarship assessment, Which sentence fairly represents an opponent's strongest concern before responding to it?
options: Anyone who questions the cost is ignorant of basic facts.
The cost is irrelevant because the proposal is well intentioned.
Critics argue that the cost may burden smaller institutions; a staged rollout could test affordability.
Critics oppose the plan because they dislike all improvements.
questions.explanation: A fair counterargument identifies a plausible concern and supplies a relevant, proportionate response.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 archival scholarship assessment, Which sentence avoids a straw-man response?
options: The critic believes no data should ever be collected.
The critic must oppose every form of scientific inquiry.
The objection is false because the critic sounds worried.
The objection concerns uncertainty in the sample, which the next study should directly address.
questions.explanation: A fair rebuttal answers the actual concern about sampling rather than misrepresenting it as total opposition.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 archival scholarship assessment, Which evidence best supports the claim that a new scheduling policy improved access?
options: Comparable participation rates before and after adoption, separated by previously underserved groups.
A slogan emphasizing the policy's fairness.
The director's biography and number of awards.
A description of the new meeting-room paint.
questions.explanation: Access must be assessed through outcomes for affected groups, not through aspirations or peripheral details.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 archival scholarship assessment, What most directly addresses external validity after a promising result in one institution?
options: Removing participants who disagree with the researcher's conclusion.
Replication in institutions with different populations and operating conditions.
A larger poster advertising the first trial.
An additional summary of the same initial observations.
questions.explanation: External validity concerns whether findings hold across relevant settings and populations.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 archival scholarship assessment, Which transition links a paragraph of favorable evidence to a paragraph about its limits?
options: For instance, the first result proves every outcome.
Likewise, no further evidence is needed.
Nevertheless, the study's restricted time frame prevents stronger conclusions.
Consequently, all uncertainty has disappeared.
questions.explanation: Nevertheless signals a contrast between encouraging findings and a meaningful qualification.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 archival scholarship assessment, Which thesis is both arguable and specific?
options: Libraries are places where people can read.
There are many different opinions about library hours.
I will discuss several interesting aspects of libraries.
A limited trial of longer library hours would help students with late obligations without requiring immediate districtwide expansion.
questions.explanation: The first thesis states a defined, debatable proposal and its rationale.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 archival scholarship assessment, Two competing explanations fit the same results. What should the next investigation prioritize?
options: A prediction on which the explanations disagree and a measurement able to test it.
More forceful repetition of the preferred explanation.
Removal of all results that appear inconsistent.
A vote to decide which explanation sounds more persuasive.
questions.explanation: A discriminating prediction tests rival hypotheses rather than relying on rhetoric or preference.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 archival scholarship assessment, Which comparison best supports evaluating an intervention's effectiveness?
options: A list of names of people who designed the intervention.
Outcomes in comparable exposed and unexposed groups, accounting for baseline differences.
A favorable anecdote collected after implementation.
The intervention's advertised purpose.
questions.explanation: A controlled comparison helps separate an intervention effect from background differences.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 archival scholarship assessment, Which assessment of a source's reliability is most defensible?
options: Accept any source repeated frequently online.
Assume all old sources are inherently accurate.
Evaluate its evidence, methods, possible incentives, and independent corroboration.
Treat professional titles as sufficient proof.
questions.explanation: Reliability depends on traceable methods and evidence rather than authority or repetition alone.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 archival scholarship assessment, Which interpretation of a historical object stays within the evidence?
options: The object proves every resident shared an identical belief.
The artifact reveals the full intentions of its maker without corroboration.
The single find establishes a universal historical law.
Its presence suggests a practice at that site, but not necessarily how widespread or intentional the practice was.
questions.explanation: A local artifact supports bounded inferences and does not establish prevalence or mental states.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 archival scholarship assessment, When is an analogy strongest as evidence?
options: When the two situations share the features relevant to the conclusion being drawn.
Whenever the situations have similar-sounding names.
Whenever a memorable story can be substituted for data.
When one case is popular, even if the relevant mechanisms differ.
questions.explanation: A valid analogy depends on the similarity of causally or logically relevant features.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 archival scholarship assessment, Which conclusion best synthesizes promising evidence and its stated limitations?
options: A positive result makes methodological details unnecessary.
The findings justify further targeted trials, not immediate certainty about every possible application.
The hypothesis has been established in every population.
The limitations prove that the evidence is worthless.
questions.explanation: A synthesis integrates support and qualification without overstating generality.

questions.text: In the day 15 mathematics full-paper case: Neither the chair nor the analysts who drafted the report ___ prepared to endorse it.
options: was
is
has been
were
questions.explanation: The nearer plural noun requires the plural verb were.

questions.text: In the day 15 mathematics full-paper case: Each of the findings that the analysts discussed ___ supported by independent evidence.
options: is
are
were
have been
questions.explanation: The singular distributive head each governs is despite the intervening plural phrase.

questions.text: In the day 15 mathematics full-paper case: By the time Noah presented the report, the review team ___ its sources.
options: is checking
had already checked
has already checked
will check
questions.explanation: Past perfect marks a completed event before another past event.

questions.text: In the day 15 mathematics full-paper case: After reviewing the contradictory evidence, ___.
options: the report was amended
the result seemed doubtful
the analysts revised their interpretation
a discrepancy became apparent
questions.explanation: The people who performed the reviewing must immediately follow the opening modifier.

questions.text: In the day 15 mathematics full-paper case: The revised interpretation was more comprehensive than ___.
options: the previous chair
the original analysts
the archive that stored the document
that in the earlier report
questions.explanation: The construction compares interpretations with interpretations, not people or institutions.

questions.text: In the day 15 mathematics full-paper case: If Noah ___ responsible for the report, the chair would seek independent confirmation.
options: were
will be
has been
is
questions.explanation: Were expresses an unreal present condition in conventional formal usage.

questions.text: In the day 15 mathematics full-paper case: The report may be accepted only if the analysts approve it. What can be inferred?

Their approval is necessary, not necessarily sufficient.
Their approval guarantees acceptance.
Acceptance may precede approval under the stated rule.
questions.explanation: Only if specifies a necessary condition and does not guarantee success.

questions.text: In the day 15 mathematics full-paper case: Which sentence identifies Noah as the person who actually inspected the evidence?
options: After she inspected it, Noah informed the chair.
The chair and Noah discussed the findings after she inspected it.
After inspecting the evidence, Noah informed the chair.
Noah informed the chair after she inspected it.
questions.explanation: The introductory modifier clearly identifies its agent in the first sentence; the other references are ambiguous.

questions.text: In the day 15 mathematics full-paper case: Which sentence means that the analysts revised no section except the conclusion?
options: Only the analysts revised the conclusion of the report.
The analysts only revised the conclusion of the report.
The analysts revised the only conclusion of the report.
The analysts revised only the conclusion of the report.
questions.explanation: Only immediately before the object narrows what was revised.

questions.text: In the day 15 mathematics full-paper case: Which sentence correctly connects two independent clauses with a conjunctive adverb?
options: The report was persuasive; nevertheless, the chair requested more evidence.
The report was persuasive, nevertheless, the chair requested more evidence.
The report was persuasive; nevertheless the chair requested more evidence.
The report was persuasive nevertheless; the chair requested more evidence.
questions.explanation: A semicolon separates the independent clauses and a comma follows nevertheless.

questions.text: In the day 15 mathematics full-paper case: The number of analysts assigned to the task ___ increased since September.
options: are
has
have
were
questions.explanation: The singular head number takes has, despite the plural noun in its complement.

questions.text: In the day 15 mathematics full-paper case: Which version accurately compares the number of unsupported claims?
options: The revised report contained least unsupported claims.
The revised report contained much fewer unsupported claims.
The revised report contained fewer unsupported claims.
The revised report contained less unsupported claims.
questions.explanation: Claims are countable, so fewer is the standard comparative.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 museum curation assessment, A number of researchers ___ raised concerns about the proposed interpretation.
options: has
is
was
have
questions.explanation: A number of followed by a plural noun takes a plural verb.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 museum curation assessment, Either the analysts or the department head ___ required to approve the final report.
options: is
are
were
have
questions.explanation: The nearest noun head is singular, so is is correct.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 museum curation assessment, Which punctuation correctly connects the two independent clauses?
options: The evidence was incomplete; and, the review continued.
The evidence was incomplete; the review continued.
The evidence was incomplete, the review continued.
The evidence was incomplete: and the review continued.
questions.explanation: A semicolon may directly join two closely related independent clauses without a coordinating conjunction.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 museum curation assessment, Which construction uses inversion correctly after the negative adverbial?
options: Not only did the committee revised its proposal but also explained.
Not only the committee had revised its proposal, but it also explaining.
Not only did the committee revise its proposal, but it also explained the change.
Not only the committee did revise its proposal, but explained also.
questions.explanation: Negative-initial not only requires auxiliary inversion in the first clause.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 museum curation assessment, Which version uses whose as a relative possessive rather than confusing it with who is?
options: The researcher who's measurements were disputed requested a review.
The researcher whose's measurements were disputed requested a review.
The researcher who measurements were disputed requested a review.
The researcher whose measurements were disputed requested a review.
questions.explanation: Whose is a possessive relative determiner; who's means who is or who has.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 museum curation assessment, Which sentence means that the director considered just one document and no others?
options: The director examined only the revised report.
Only the director examined the revised report.
The director only examined the revised report.
The director examined the only revised report.
questions.explanation: Only modifies the immediately following object 'the revised report' to restrict the documents examined.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 museum curation assessment, Which comparison preserves the intended grammatical structure?
options: The second analysis was most rigorous as the first.
The second analysis was as rigorous as the first analysis.
The second analysis was as more rigorous as the first.
The second analysis was so rigorous than the first.
questions.explanation: The equality comparison follows as + adjective + as.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 museum curation assessment, Which quantifier correctly describes a reduced amount of uncertainty, treated as an uncountable quantity?
options: The revised model left least uncertainty than before.
The revised model left many less uncertainty.
The revised model left less uncertainty.
The revised model left fewer uncertainty.
questions.explanation: Uncertainty is mass-noun usage here, requiring less rather than fewer.

The technician lain the instruments on the table yesterday.
The technician lies the instruments on the table yesterday.
The technician laid the instruments on the table before leaving.
questions.explanation: Laid is the past tense of transitive lay and takes the direct object instruments.

The appendix provides evidence that compliments the argument.
The appendix provides evidence that complement's the argument.
The appendix provides evidence that compliment the argument.
questions.explanation: The verb complement means to complete or enhance; compliment means praise.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 museum curation assessment, Which sentence consistently reports a past claim without an illogical tense shift?
options: The editor said that the committee had reviews the evidence before publishing.
The editor said that the committee had reviewed the evidence before publishing.
The editor said that the committee will have reviewed the evidence yesterday.
The editor said that the committee review the evidence before it published.
questions.explanation: Past reporting combines naturally with a past perfect for an earlier action.

options: The three finalists, who had all submitted their work awaited the decision.
The three finalists who had all submitted their work awaited, the decision.
The three finalists, who had all submitted their work, awaited the decision.
The three finalists who had all submitted their work, awaited the decision.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 museum curation assessment, Which punctuation correctly marks the introductory dependent clause?
options: Although the data appeared consistent the team, requested replication.
Although, the data appeared consistent the team requested replication.
Although the data, appeared consistent the team requested replication.
Although the data appeared consistent, the team requested replication.
questions.explanation: A dependent opening clause is followed by a comma before the main clause.

The team evaluated not only the methods but also evaluating the assumptions.
The team evaluated not only the methods but also to assess the assumptions.

questions.text: In the day 17 engineering full-paper case: A preliminary observation in engineering was positive. Which conclusion is appropriately calibrated?

An announcement praising the procedure's designers.

questions.text: In the day 17 engineering full-paper case: Which sentence makes a concession without abandoning the argument?

The intervention is correct because its supporters are enthusiastic.
Although implementation may be costly, a limited pilot could test whether the benefits justify that expense.
questions.explanation: The concession admits a legitimate cost while proposing evidence to evaluate the trade-off.

questions.text: In the day 17 engineering full-paper case: Which additional method would most reduce uncertainty about a causal claim in engineering?

Replace the results section with a more confident abstract.
Repeat the same conclusion in several paragraphs.
Remove inconvenient outliers without documenting them.
questions.explanation: Addressing confounding and selection can distinguish a causal relationship from a misleading association.

questions.text: In the day 17 engineering full-paper case: Which transition best introduces a limitation following positive results?

In other words, a favorable result guarantees universal success.
questions.explanation: Nevertheless marks a meaningful qualification to apparently promising evidence.

An unrelated dated record supports the same chronology.
The original author repeats the claim in a later paragraph.
questions.explanation: Independent supporting material is stronger corroboration than restating the same unsupported source.

The researchers interviewed every official.
The volunteers adequately represent the wider population.
questions.explanation: Extrapolating from volunteers assumes they do not differ systematically from the broader public.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 transportation research assessment, Which interpretation avoids the post hoc fallacy when a policy change precedes an improvement?

The earlier policy change necessarily caused the improvement.
Every improvement must follow from the most recent change.
Temporal order invalidates all observational evidence.
questions.explanation: Temporal sequence is necessary for many causal accounts but cannot alone identify the cause.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 transportation research assessment, Which sentence fairly represents an opponent's strongest concern before responding to it?

Critics oppose the plan because they dislike all improvements.
Anyone who questions the cost is ignorant of basic facts.
questions.explanation: A fair counterargument identifies a plausible concern and supplies a relevant, proportionate response.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 transportation research assessment, Which sentence avoids a straw-man response?

The objection is false because the critic sounds worried.
The objection concerns uncertainty in the sample, which the next study should directly address.
The critic believes no data should ever be collected.
questions.explanation: A fair rebuttal answers the actual concern about sampling rather than misrepresenting it as total opposition.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 transportation research assessment, Which evidence best supports the claim that a new scheduling policy improved access?

The director's biography and number of awards.
A description of the new meeting-room paint.
Comparable participation rates before and after adoption, separated by previously underserved groups.
questions.explanation: Access must be assessed through outcomes for affected groups, not through aspirations or peripheral details.

Removing participants who disagree with the researcher's conclusion.
questions.explanation: External validity concerns whether findings hold across relevant settings and populations.

Nevertheless, the study's restricted time frame prevents stronger conclusions.

For instance, the first result proves every outcome.
questions.explanation: Nevertheless signals a contrast between encouraging findings and a meaningful qualification.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 transportation research assessment, Which thesis is both arguable and specific?

I will discuss several interesting aspects of libraries.
A limited trial of longer library hours would help students with late obligations without requiring immediate districtwide expansion.
Libraries are places where people can read.
questions.explanation: The first thesis states a defined, debatable proposal and its rationale.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 transportation research assessment, Two competing explanations fit the same results. What should the next investigation prioritize?

Removal of all results that appear inconsistent.
A vote to decide which explanation sounds more persuasive.
A prediction on which the explanations disagree and a measurement able to test it.
questions.explanation: A discriminating prediction tests rival hypotheses rather than relying on rhetoric or preference.

The appendix provides evidence that complements the argument.
The appendix provides evidence that compliments the argument.
The appendix provides evidence that complement's the argument.
questions.explanation: The verb complement means to complete or enhance; compliment means praise.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 linguistic analysis assessment, Which sentence consistently reports a past claim without an illogical tense shift?
options: The editor said that the committee review the evidence before it published.
The editor said that the committee had reviews the evidence before publishing.
The editor said that the committee had reviewed the evidence before publishing.
The editor said that the committee will have reviewed the evidence yesterday.
questions.explanation: Past reporting combines naturally with a past perfect for an earlier action.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 linguistic analysis assessment, Which sentence correctly treats the relative clause as additional, nonrestrictive information about a known group?
options: The three finalists who had all submitted their work, awaited the decision.
The three finalists, who had all submitted their work awaited the decision.
The three finalists who had all submitted their work awaited, the decision.
The three finalists, who had all submitted their work, awaited the decision.
questions.explanation: A nonrestrictive clause is bracketed by commas and does not select only some of the known finalists.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 linguistic analysis assessment, Which version makes the introductory action's agent unambiguous?
options: Having reviewed the transcript, the historian corrected the chronology.
Having reviewed the transcript, the chronology was corrected.
After studying the archive, a discrepancy appeared.
Having read the transcript, the report's conclusions changed.
questions.explanation: The historian is the following subject and therefore performs the reviewing.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 linguistic analysis assessment, Which version appropriately uses were to express an unreal present condition?
options: The committee spoke as if the outcome be already certainty.
The committee spoke as if the outcome were already certain.
The committee spoke as if the outcome will already certain.
The committee spoke as if the outcome had certain yesterday.
questions.explanation: Were marks a contrary-to-fact or hypothetical state in formal usage.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 linguistic analysis assessment, Neither of the proposed interpretations ___ supported by the available data.
options: were
have
is
are
questions.explanation: Neither is grammatically singular in this formal construction.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 linguistic analysis assessment, Which question correctly uses whom in a formal object position?
options: Whom submitted the final report?
Whom was responsible for the analysis?
Whom have been approved for the hearing?
Whom did the panel invite to testify?
questions.explanation: Whom is the object of invite; the other questions need subject-case who.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 linguistic analysis assessment, Which punctuation correctly marks the introductory dependent clause?
options: Although the data appeared consistent, the team requested replication.
Although the data appeared consistent the team, requested replication.
Although, the data appeared consistent the team requested replication.
Although the data, appeared consistent the team requested replication.
questions.explanation: A dependent opening clause is followed by a comma before the main clause.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 linguistic analysis assessment, Which sentence maintains parallel objects with not only...but also?
options: The team evaluated not only the methods but also to assess the assumptions.
The team evaluated not only the methods but also the underlying assumptions.
The team not only evaluated the methods but also the underlying assumptions.
The team evaluated not only the methods but also evaluating the assumptions.
questions.explanation: Both correlatives introduce parallel noun phrases serving as objects of evaluated.

questions.text: In the day 20 urban history full-paper case: A preliminary observation in urban history was positive. Which conclusion is appropriately calibrated?
options: The evidence is encouraging, but different settings should be tested before generalizing.
The observation proves the technique works everywhere.
All alternative explanations are now impossible.
One positive result demonstrates a permanent causal mechanism.
questions.explanation: A preliminary observation supports a provisional inference rather than a universal conclusion.

questions.text: In the day 20 urban history full-paper case: Which evidence would best establish that a new procedure reduced errors in urban history?
options: The number of pages in the final report.
A comparison of verified error rates under comparable conditions.
An announcement praising the procedure's designers.
A description of the room where the procedure originated.
questions.explanation: Comparable error-rate measurements directly test the alleged improvement.

questions.text: In the day 20 urban history full-paper case: Which sentence makes a concession without abandoning the argument?
options: The intervention cannot possibly have drawbacks.
The intervention is correct because its supporters are enthusiastic.
Although implementation may be costly, a limited pilot could test whether the benefits justify that expense.
The intervention costs money, so the idea must be rejected.
questions.explanation: The concession admits a legitimate cost while proposing evidence to evaluate the trade-off.

questions.text: In the day 20 urban history full-paper case: Which additional method would most reduce uncertainty about a causal claim in urban history?
options: Replace the results section with a more confident abstract.
Repeat the same conclusion in several paragraphs.
Remove inconvenient outliers without documenting them.
Identify selection effects and plausible confounding variables.
questions.explanation: Addressing confounding and selection can distinguish a causal relationship from a misleading association.

questions.text: In the day 20 urban history full-paper case: Which transition best introduces a limitation following positive results?
options: Nevertheless, the data cover too short a period to establish a lasting trend.
Therefore, every other hypothesis is impossible.
In other words, a favorable result guarantees universal success.
Similarly, no further investigation is necessary.
questions.explanation: Nevertheless marks a meaningful qualification to apparently promising evidence.

questions.text: In the day 20 urban history full-paper case: Which finding would independently corroborate a disputed historical claim in urban history?
options: A popular account asserts the story is interesting.
An unrelated dated record supports the same chronology.
The original author repeats the claim in a later paragraph.
Several summaries quote the same anonymous assertion.
questions.explanation: Independent supporting material is stronger corroboration than restating the same unsupported source.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 linguistic analysis assessment, What unstated assumption is required to infer public opinion from a volunteer survey?
options: The survey report contains at least two paragraphs.
The researchers interviewed every official.
The volunteers adequately represent the wider population.
All respondents prefer answering surveys.
questions.explanation: Extrapolating from volunteers assumes they do not differ systematically from the broader public.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 linguistic analysis assessment, Which interpretation avoids the post hoc fallacy when a policy change precedes an improvement?
options: The earlier policy change necessarily caused the improvement.
Every improvement must follow from the most recent change.
Temporal order invalidates all observational evidence.
The sequence is consistent with causation but does not establish it without ruling out alternative causes.
questions.explanation: Temporal sequence is necessary for many causal accounts but cannot alone identify the cause.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 linguistic analysis assessment, Which sentence fairly represents an opponent's strongest concern before responding to it?
options: Critics argue that the cost may burden smaller institutions; a staged rollout could test affordability.
Critics oppose the plan because they dislike all improvements.
Anyone who questions the cost is ignorant of basic facts.
The cost is irrelevant because the proposal is well intentioned.
questions.explanation: A fair counterargument identifies a plausible concern and supplies a relevant, proportionate response.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 linguistic analysis assessment, Which sentence avoids a straw-man response?
options: The objection is false because the critic sounds worried.
The objection concerns uncertainty in the sample, which the next study should directly address.
The critic believes no data should ever be collected.
The critic must oppose every form of scientific inquiry.
questions.explanation: A fair rebuttal answers the actual concern about sampling rather than misrepresenting it as total opposition.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 linguistic analysis assessment, Which evidence best supports the claim that a new scheduling policy improved access?
options: The director's biography and number of awards.
A description of the new meeting-room paint.
Comparable participation rates before and after adoption, separated by previously underserved groups.
A slogan emphasizing the policy's fairness.
questions.explanation: Access must be assessed through outcomes for affected groups, not through aspirations or peripheral details.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 linguistic analysis assessment, What most directly addresses external validity after a promising result in one institution?
options: A larger poster advertising the first trial.
An additional summary of the same initial observations.
Removing participants who disagree with the researcher's conclusion.
Replication in institutions with different populations and operating conditions.
questions.explanation: External validity concerns whether findings hold across relevant settings and populations.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 linguistic analysis assessment, Which transition links a paragraph of favorable evidence to a paragraph about its limits?
options: Nevertheless, the study's restricted time frame prevents stronger conclusions.
Consequently, all uncertainty has disappeared.
For instance, the first result proves every outcome.
Likewise, no further evidence is needed.
questions.explanation: Nevertheless signals a contrast between encouraging findings and a meaningful qualification.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 linguistic analysis assessment, Which thesis is both arguable and specific?
options: I will discuss several interesting aspects of libraries.
A limited trial of longer library hours would help students with late obligations without requiring immediate districtwide expansion.
Libraries are places where people can read.
There are many different opinions about library hours.
questions.explanation: The first thesis states a defined, debatable proposal and its rationale.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 linguistic analysis assessment, Two competing explanations fit the same results. What should the next investigation prioritize?
options: Removal of all results that appear inconsistent.
A vote to decide which explanation sounds more persuasive.
A prediction on which the explanations disagree and a measurement able to test it.
More forceful repetition of the preferred explanation.
questions.explanation: A discriminating prediction tests rival hypotheses rather than relying on rhetoric or preference.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 linguistic analysis assessment, Which comparison best supports evaluating an intervention's effectiveness?
options: A favorable anecdote collected after implementation.
The intervention's advertised purpose.
A list of names of people who designed the intervention.
Outcomes in comparable exposed and unexposed groups, accounting for baseline differences.
questions.explanation: A controlled comparison helps separate an intervention effect from background differences.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 linguistic analysis assessment, Which assessment of a source's reliability is most defensible?
options: Evaluate its evidence, methods, possible incentives, and independent corroboration.
Treat professional titles as sufficient proof.
Accept any source repeated frequently online.
Assume all old sources are inherently accurate.
questions.explanation: Reliability depends on traceable methods and evidence rather than authority or repetition alone.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 linguistic analysis assessment, Which interpretation of a historical object stays within the evidence?
options: The single find establishes a universal historical law.
Its presence suggests a practice at that site, but not necessarily how widespread or intentional the practice was.
The object proves every resident shared an identical belief.
The artifact reveals the full intentions of its maker without corroboration.
questions.explanation: A local artifact supports bounded inferences and does not establish prevalence or mental states.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 linguistic analysis assessment, When is an analogy strongest as evidence?
options: Whenever a memorable story can be substituted for data.
When one case is popular, even if the relevant mechanisms differ.
When the two situations share the features relevant to the conclusion being drawn.
Whenever the situations have similar-sounding names.
questions.explanation: A valid analogy depends on the similarity of causally or logically relevant features.

questions.text: For a grade 10–12 linguistic analysis assessment, Which conclusion best synthesizes promising evidence and its stated limitations?
options: The hypothesis has been established in every population.
The limitations prove that the evidence is worthless.
A positive result makes methodological details unnecessary.
The findings justify further targeted trials, not immediate certainty about every possible application.
questions.explanation: A synthesis integrates support and qualification without overstating generality.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy guided-practice case: The memorandum may be accepted only if the editors approve it. What can be inferred?

Their approval is necessary, not necessarily sufficient.
Their approval guarantees acceptance.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy guided-practice case: Which sentence identifies Dr. Anika as the person who actually inspected the evidence?
options: After she inspected it, Dr. Anika informed the director.

Dr. Anika informed the director after she inspected it.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy guided-practice case: Which sentence means that the editors revised no section except the conclusion?

The editors revised only the conclusion of the memorandum.
questions.explanation: Only immediately before the object narrows what was revised.

questions.text: In the day 1 astronomy guided-practice case: Which sentence correctly connects two independent clauses with a conjunctive adverb?

The memorandum was persuasive, nevertheless, the director requested more evidence.
The memorandum was persuasive; nevertheless the director requested more evidence.
The memorandum was persuasive nevertheless; the director requested more evidence.
questions.explanation: A semicolon separates the independent clauses and a comma follows nevertheless.
